learn.hook: The rain that fell on your school today may once have been in the sea, a cloud, or even a leaf! How does water travel?
points: The Sun heats water in seas, rivers, lakes and ponds. The water slowly turns into water vapour and rises. This is evaporation.
High up in the sky, the air is cooler. Water vapour cools and turns into tiny water droplets. This is condensation. Many droplets together form clouds.
When the droplets join and become big and heavy, they fall as rain, snow or hail. This is precipitation.
Rainwater flows into rivers, lakes and seas, and some soaks into the ground. Then the cycle starts again.
Plants also give out water vapour from their leaves. This is called transpiration.

example.q: Meena hangs wet clothes in the sun at 9 a.m. By noon they are dry. Where did the water go?
steps: The Sun warmed the wet clothes.
The water in them turned into water vapour.
The vapour mixed with the air. We cannot see water vapour.
example.answer: The water evaporated into the air as water vapour.

learn.reallife: Drying clothes, a puddle vanishing after rain, and drops on a cold glass of nimbu paani are all parts of the water cycle around you.

games.title: Round and round
games.prompt: Put the steps of the water cycle in order, starting from the sea
items: Sun heats water in the sea
Water turns into vapour and rises
Vapour cools and forms clouds
Rain falls from heavy clouds
Rainwater flows back to rivers and the sea

quiz.q: What do we call the change of water into water vapour when it is heated?
quiz.explain: When water is heated, it turns into water vapour and rises into the air. This is evaporation.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up evaporation with condensation, which is the opposite change

quiz.q: Tiny water droplets collect high in the sky. What do they form?
quiz.explain: Millions of tiny droplets of water together make a cloud.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect clouds with water droplets

quiz.q: Which gives the heat that drives the water cycle?
quiz.explain: The Sun heats water on Earth so that it evaporates. Without the Sun's heat, the cycle would stop.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Moon or wind heats the water

quiz.q: Ravi takes a cold bottle out of the fridge. Soon tiny drops appear on the outside. Where did they come from?
options: Water leaked out through the bottle
The fridge sprayed water on it
Water vapour in the air cooled on the bottle
quiz.explain: Air has water vapour in it. It cools when it touches the cold bottle and turns into drops. This is condensation.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the water seeped through the closed bottle

quiz.q: Rain, snow and hail falling from clouds are all called what?
quiz.explain: Any water that falls from clouds to the ground is called precipitation.
quiz.mistake: Uses the word for a different step of the cycle

quiz.q: Plants give out water vapour through tiny holes in their leaves. What is this called?
quiz.explain: Leaves lose water as vapour to the air. This is transpiration, and it adds water to the water cycle.
quiz.mistake: Does not know plants are part of the water cycle

quiz.q: When will a puddle on the road dry fastest?
options: On a hot, sunny and windy day
quiz.explain: Heat and wind both make water evaporate faster, so a hot, sunny, windy day dries a puddle quickest.
quiz.mistake: Does not link heat and wind with faster evaporation

quiz.q: Why is the water cycle called a 'cycle'?
options: It happens only once a year
Water is used up and lost forever
Water keeps moving round and round between Earth and sky
quiz.explain: Water evaporates, forms clouds, falls as rain and returns to seas again and again. So it is a cycle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks water is used up instead of moving in a loop

teach.ask: Gappu tilts his head: 'Where does rain come from? Who fills the clouds?'
teach.praise: Wow! So the Sun lifts water up, clouds form, and rain brings it back. What a clever loop!
teach.nudge: But how does the water get up into the sky? And what happens up there to make clouds?

learn.hook: You can live for weeks without food, but only a few days without water. Why is water so special?
points: All living things need water: people, animals and plants.
Water helps us digest food, keeps our body cool and carries waste out of the body. More than half of our body weight is water.
We use water for drinking, cooking, bathing, washing, farming and in factories.
Water covers about three-fourths of the Earth's surface, but most of it is salty sea water. Only a tiny part is fresh water we can use.
We get fresh water from rain, rivers, lakes, ponds, wells and from under the ground (groundwater).

example.q: Our Earth has so much water. Why do people still say there is a shortage of water?
steps: Most of Earth's water is in seas and is salty.
A lot of the fresh water is frozen as ice.
So the water we can drink is only a small part.
example.answer: Because only a very small part of Earth's water is fresh water that we can use.

learn.reallife: In summer, people put out bowls of water for birds and set up 'pyaau' (free drinking water stalls) for travellers. Water is life!

games.title: Water facts
items: Plants need water to make their food.
Plants use water, sunlight and air to make food in their leaves.
Most of the water on Earth is fresh water we can drink.
Most of Earth's water is salty sea water.
Water from under the ground is called groundwater.
Rainwater soaks into the soil and collects underground.
Our body does not need water if we eat enough food.
We must drink water every day; our body cannot work without it.
Farmers need water to grow crops.
Crops like rice and wheat need water to grow.

quiz.q: A cactus grows in the dry desert. Does it need water?
options: Yes, it needs a little water to live
It needs water only in winter
quiz.explain: A cactus stores water in its thick stem and needs very little, but like every living thing it still needs water.
quiz.mistake: Thinks desert plants need no water at all

quiz.q: Most of the water on Earth is found in
quiz.explain: Seas and oceans hold most of Earth's water, and that water is salty.
quiz.mistake: Thinks wells or ponds hold most water because we see them more

quiz.q: Why can't we drink sea water?
options: It has no water in it
quiz.explain: Sea water has a lot of salt dissolved in it. It is not fit for drinking.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the colour or temperature makes it unsafe

quiz.q: Water that is stored under the ground is called
quiz.explain: Rainwater seeps into the soil and is stored under the ground. It is called groundwater.
quiz.mistake: Confuses where the water is stored with where it came from

quiz.q: Which of these takes out groundwater for us to use?
quiz.explain: Hand pumps, wells and borewells bring up water from under the ground.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which things reach water underground

quiz.q: How does water help our body?
options: It makes our bones from stone
It helps digest food and keeps us cool
quiz.explain: Water helps digestion, keeps our body temperature right and removes waste through sweat and urine.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the jobs water does in the body

quiz.q: How much of the Earth's surface is covered by water?
quiz.explain: About three-fourths of the Earth's surface is water. That is why Earth looks blue from space.
quiz.mistake: Guesses from the amount of land seen around them

quiz.q: Which is the best way to make muddy drinking water safer at home?
options: Keep it in the sun in an open bucket
Filter it and then boil it
quiz.explain: Filtering removes dirt and boiling kills germs, so the water becomes safer to drink.
quiz.mistake: Thinks clear-looking or stirred water is safe

teach.ask: Gappu sips from a leaf: 'Why does everyone say water is precious? There is so much of it!'
teach.praise: Oh! Most water is salty and only a little is fresh. And every living thing needs it. I will never waste a drop!
teach.nudge: But can we drink all that sea water? And who needs water to live?

learn.hook: If every family in your colony saved one bucket of water a day, that would fill a whole tank in a week. Small steps make big savings!
points: We waste water when taps leak, when we leave taps running, or when we let rainwater just flow away.
Rainwater harvesting means collecting rainwater from rooftops and storing it, or sending it into the ground.
Long ago, people in India built stepwells (called baoli or vav), ponds and tanks to store water. Rani ki Vav in Gujarat is a famous stepwell.
In the desert of Rajasthan, people built covered pits called kunds or tankas to collect rainwater. Johads are small earthen dams that hold rainwater.
We can reuse water: water used to wash vegetables or rice can water the plants.

example.q: Aarav brushes his teeth for 2 minutes with the tap running. What can he do to save water?
steps: The tap does not need to run while he brushes.
He can fill a mug and use only that water.
He turns the tap off until he needs to rinse.
example.answer: Use a mug of water and keep the tap closed while brushing.

learn.reallife: Many housing societies and schools in cities like Chennai and Bengaluru have rooftop rainwater harvesting. Look for pipes that carry roof water into a tank or pit!

quiz.q: What is rainwater harvesting?
options: Collecting and storing rainwater for later use
Growing crops only in the rain
quiz.explain: Rainwater harvesting means catching rainwater, for example from rooftops, and storing it or sending it into the ground.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'harvesting' only means cutting crops

quiz.q: Rani ki Vav, a beautiful old stepwell, is in which state?
quiz.explain: Rani ki Vav is in Patan, Gujarat. 'Vav' is the Gujarati word for a stepwell.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a state without linking 'vav' to Gujarat

quiz.q: Why did people build kunds in the Thar Desert?
options: To collect and store the little rain that falls
quiz.explain: The desert gets very little rain, so people built kunds to save every drop for drinking.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect kunds with water storage

quiz.q: Which habit saves the most water while bathing?
options: Using a shower for a long time
quiz.explain: A bucket bath uses a fixed amount of water, so less water is wasted.
quiz.mistake: Thinks long showers use less water

quiz.q: Water used for washing vegetables can be reused to
quiz.explain: This water is a little dirty but fine for plants. We should not drink or cook with it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks used water is fine for drinking

quiz.q: A johad is
options: a small earthen dam that holds rainwater
quiz.explain: Johads are small mud dams built across slopes to stop and store rainwater. They help water soak into the ground.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a johad with other water objects

quiz.q: Rainwater sent into a pit in the ground helps to
quiz.explain: Water soaking into the ground refills the groundwater, so wells and hand pumps have water later.
quiz.mistake: Does not know rainwater can refill groundwater

quiz.q: World Water Day is celebrated every year on
quiz.explain: World Water Day is on 22 March. It reminds everyone to save and value water.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with World Environment Day on 5 June

teach.ask: Gappu splashes in a puddle: 'How can I save water? Can you teach me some ways?'
teach.praise: Hooray! Close the tap, reuse water and collect the rain. My nest will save water too!
teach.nudge: Good start! But what about the rain? How can we catch and store rainwater?
